articles.title: Shivraj Singh Chouhan to unveil India's first indigenous bird flu vaccine on Nov 20
articles.content: Shivraj Singh Chouhan to unveil India's first indigenous bird flu vaccine on Nov 20 IANS November 18, 2026 10:13 AM Share on | New Delhi, Nov 18 (IANS) Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan is set to unveil India’s first indigenous ‘Inactivated H5N1’ avian influenza (bird flu) vaccine for chickens on November 20, an official statement said on Wednesday. The highly pathogenic avian influenza vaccine for chickens, developed by ICAR-NIHSAD Bhopal, aims to provide protection against ‘Clade 2.3.2.1a H5N1’ virus strains circulating in the country. At present, no specific commercial vaccine is available against the H5N1 virus of Clade 2.3.2.1a. Therefore, developing an indigenous vaccine is important for India. Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza (HPAI), commonly known as bird flu, is a serious disease affecting poultry. Outbreaks can cause nearly 100 per cent mortality among infected birds, leading to major financial losses for poultry farmers due to the large-scale culling of birds and restrictions on trade. The impact is not limited to poultry farms; it can also affect global trade, prices of poultry products, and the livelihoods of farmers. Since the first detection of the disease in India in 2006, more than 500 combined outbreaks of H5N1 and H5N8 subtypes have been reported in the country, according to Agriculture Ministry. A major outbreak of bird flu could reduce India's GDP growth by up to 1.5 per cent, while more than 20 per cent of the country's poultry population could be at risk if the disease spreads without control. The 2006 bird flu outbreak caused estimated direct and indirect losses of Rs 2,200–3,000 crore. An outbreak in Manipur also resulted in losses equivalent to 0.5 per cent of the state's GDP. The disease is also a public health concern. According to the World Health Organization (WHO), 1,003 human cases of H5N1 avian influenza, including 479 deaths, have been reported across 25 countries, including India, since 2003. Studies have shown that the H5N1 strain known as Clade 2.3.2.1a has been responsible for most bird flu outbreaks in chickens. In recent times, infections caused by this strain have also been detected in different animal species, including mammals, along with three human cases. This makes it important to control the spread of this virus to reduce financial losses for poultry farmers and prevent its transmission from chickens to other animals and humans, said the statement. —IANS na/

articles.title: CM Shivakumar pitches Karnataka as global AI hub - The New Indian Express
articles.content: BENGALURU: Chief Minister D K Shivakumar pitched Karnataka as a global hub for artificial intelligence, deep technology, semiconductor manufacturing and biotechnology, backed by progressive policies, strong research institutions, a thriving startup ecosystem and skilled human resources. Speaking at the inauguration of the 29th edition of the Bengaluru Tech Summit, themed ‘AI and Beyond’, the Chief Minister said Karnataka had consistently been at the forefront of technological advancement and was now preparing to lead the next phase of global innovation. He said Bengaluru had evolved into one of the world’s largest technology clusters by embracing talent, diversity and ambition from across the globe, and some of India’s most ambitious scientific and engineering projects have found a home in Karnataka. Alluding to Karnataka’s contribution to India’s technology economy, Shivakumar said that the state accounted for two out of every five dollars earned by India through software and services exports, amounting to approximately $ 173 billion in 2025. Karnataka received $ 9.4 billion in FDI equity inflows in the first half of FY 2025-26, accounting for 26.7 per cent of India’s total inflows. “More than 1,000 Global Capability Centres (GCCs) had chosen Bengaluru as their base, with over 30 new GCCs bringing investments exceeding $ 1 billion into the State in 2025 alone”, the CM informed. Citing Karnataka’s scientific achievements, he drew references to Chandrayaan-3, the digital identity platform developed at IIIT-Bengaluru, Biocon’s global pharmaceutical reach and Bengaluru-based Sarvam’s role in developing India’s own AI model. The state has more than 24,000 recognised startups, with nearly two out of every five Indian unicorns originating from Karnataka. Bengaluru ranked eighth among the world’s startup ecosystems and second in Asia for AI-native startups. It attracted $ 4.4 billion in technology funding, nearly matching the $ 4.8 billion raised by the next five Indian cities combined, while Karnataka startups have collectively raised USD 79 billion, he said. He added that women start-up founders in Bengaluru had secured $ 13.4 billion in funds. Describing AI as the foundation of Karnataka’s next phase of technological development, Shivakumar said Bengaluru accounted for nearly 50 per cent of India’s AI and machine-learning talent. He said the government was building India’s first government-driven AI University, with an AI Hub at its centre to bring startups, researchers and industry together. “An additional Centre of Excellence at IIIT Raichur would extend AI applications to the 13 districts of North Karnataka, with solutions for agriculture, healthcare, education and small businesses,” he said. On semiconductor development, Shivakumar said Karnataka was home to more than 100 fabless chip companies, while three out of every five engineers working in India’s semiconductor capability centres were based in Bengaluru. He remarked that the state accounted for one-fifth of India’s electronics exports and was now moving from semiconductor design towards manufacturing. Global companies were investing more than Rs 23,000 crore in semiconductor research and manufacturing facilities in Bengaluru and Mysuru, he further added. articles.title: Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 Opens With Karnataka's AI Push - Urban Acres
articles.content: Home Breaking News Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 Opens With Karnataka’s AI Push Breaking News Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 Opens With Karnataka’s AI Push By Tenzin Choden November 17, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar inaugurated the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit on Tuesday, positioning the state as a major hub for artificial intelligence, deep technology, semiconductor manufacturing and biotechnology. The summit, themed “AI and Beyond”, is being attended by participants from more than 75 countries, up from 57 last year. Shivakumar said Karnataka’s technology strategy would build on its research institutions, startup ecosystem, skilled workforce and policies aimed at attracting global investment. He said the state accounted for two out of every five dollars earned by India through software and services exports, valued at approximately USD 173 billion last year. The Chief Minister also cited USD 9.4 billion in foreign direct investment equity inflows into Karnataka during the first half of financial year 2025-26. That represented 26.7 per cent of India’s total FDI equity inflows during the period, according to figures presented at the summit. Bengaluru is home to more than 1,000 Global Capability Centres, while over 30 new centres brought investments exceeding USD 1 billion into Karnataka in 2025, Shivakumar said. The state has more than 24,000 recognised startups, and nearly two out of every five Indian unicorns originated there. Bengaluru-based technology companies attracted USD 4.4 billion in funding, while startups across Karnataka had collectively raised approximately USD 79 billion. The state government is using grants and dedicated programmes to support deep-technology ventures. Under the ELEVATE NxT initiative, eligible ventures can receive grants of up to Rs 1 crore. Shivakumar said 33 startups had received equity-free funding totalling Rs 30 crore since last year. The government’s Innoverse deep-tech accelerator is expected to support 35 growth-stage ventures over the next five years. The government is also building what Shivakumar described as “India’s first government-driven AI University”, along with an AI Hub intended to bring startups, researchers and industry together. A Centre of Excellence at IIIT Raichur will extend artificial intelligence applications to 13 districts in North Karnataka, linking the state’s technology push to areas beyond Bengaluru. Semiconductor manufacturing and research form another part of the state’s investment pitch. Shivakumar said global companies were investing more than Rs 23,000 crore in research and manufacturing facilities in Bengaluru and Mysuru. Four electronics manufacturing clusters are planned to provide infrastructure, land, power and skilled talent for the sector. The announcements show how Karnataka is combining Bengaluru’s established software and startup base with newer priorities in AI, electronics and deep technology. They also place public research institutions, funding programmes and physical industrial infrastructure at the centre of the state’s effort to build the next phase of its technology economy. Declaring the summit open, Shivakumar invited global investors and innovators to partner with Karnataka, saying the state would provide “the talent, the policies and the partnership”.
